heroHeadline: CDC and FDA Declare America's Largest Cyclospora Outbreak Over — 12,883 Illnesses, Contamination Source Still Unresolved
heroSubtitle: CDC and FDA declared the multistate Cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms de México iceberg lettuce over on Sept 11, closing the investigation at 12,883 lab-confirmed illnesses, at least 570 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths across 21 states — up from 11,458 illnesses, 495 hospitalizations, and 20 states as of Aug 27, and now the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak on record in the U.S. Officials say the recalled lettuce is off the market and poses no further risk, but FDA's root-cause investigation into how the lettuce became contaminated remains open, with the agency still unable to explain how the parasite reached the product in sufficient quantity to sicken so many people. The closure applies only to this specific multistate outbreak; CDC's broader season-wide surveillance total (19,595 confirmed cases as of Sept 8) is a separate, larger figure that is not affected by today's announcement.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
